title: SQL Aliases
text:
SQL
Aliases



SQL Aliases

SQL aliases are used to give a column or a table a temporary name.

Aliases are used to make column names more readable.

An alias only exists for the duration of that query.

An alias is created with the
AS
keyword.

Alias for Columns

The following SQL creates two aliases, one for the CustomerID
column and one for the CustomerName column:

Syntax

Alias for column:

SELECT
column_name
AS
alias_name
FROM
table_name;

Alias for table:

SELECT
column_name(s)
FROM
table_name
AS
alias_name;

Alias for Tables

The same rules applies when you want to use an alias for a table.

It might seem useless to use aliases on tables, but when you are joining tables,
it makes sense.

Aliases are useful when:

There are more than one table involved in a query

Functions are used in the query

Column names are long or not very readable

Two or more columns are combined together
